text: A rental receipt of a deed in lieu buy-back is matched to INSTALLMENT of LOV-MATCH, because the list holds no value that names a rental and a new value would change a closed list.
why: The legacy story and the FSD say the rental is matched to its case and the TSD fixes the list, but no source maps a rental to a match value.
read: TSD P8 T3.2; FSD P8 A2.9; RWB-E4-048 AC1
confirm: Business analyst, P8, with the owner of LOV-MATCH
impact: One list member and one match state; if a RENTAL value is added later, the record and the event carry it without a schema change.

text: The rental amount, the debit day and the due date arrive through the rental read of rwb-treatment, and its name, path and field names are settled with that service before the build; until then the story and the profile carry the placeholder.
why: FEAT-TRT-16 and R-DIL-32 create the rental record and set the auto-debit in rwb-treatment, and no source in the read set publishes that read.
read: FSD P8 A2.9 (prerequisite FEAT-TRT-16); TSD P8 T5.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIL-32
confirm: Solution architect, with the S2 contract owner
impact: The rental read is consumed and faked; no rental fact is stored in rwb_payment.

text: The rental arm runs as a step of the JOB-07 event-started run started by the AceDataReady event, so the key adds no job, no Schedule and no workflow of its own.
why: The ownership rows of P8 hold JOB-07 and JOB-08 and no workflow, and the legacy Quartz marker becomes an event-started run in the target.
read: _work/msr/context/P8.md (Jobs JOB-07, JOB-08; Workflows none); Architecture v5 slide 44
impact: No Schedule, no Quartz row and no shared job table; the due date is a fact of the rental read.

text: The four reads the rental arm consumes - the rental read, the receipt and batch read, the case answer and the package read - are class C dependencies in fact, are built against their owners' published contracts and fakes from Day 1, and are carried in sections 12.2 and 13 rather than in the metadata row the plan fixes at None.
why: The plan's C row is empty while the behaviour needs four answers, and a CON story has no build dependency by rule.
read: WP B2-P8-005 story JSON (C []); Template and Rules R5.4, R5.7; TSD P8 T5.2
confirm: Solution architect, with the four contract owners
impact: The lane and the Day-1 start are unchanged; no C dependency blocks the build.

text: The auto-debit instruction to ATS and AMIS stays with FEAT-TRT-16 in rwb-treatment, which creates the rental record and sets the debit under R-DIL-32, and rwb-payment takes the debit facts from the ACE batch, issues the receipt and follows up the arrears.
why: The FSD places the instruction with ATS and AMIS and the TSD of the same module lists only ALS and GL, so one of the two must be read as the instruction's owner.
read: FSD P8 A2.9.2; TSD P8 T5.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIL-32
confirm: Solution architect, with the owners of rwb-treatment and rwb-integration
impact: No outbound instruction is built in this service; no ATS or AMIS interface is declared here.

text: The rental contract profile is additive on the base surface that RWB-P8-E4043-CON declares: it adds the rental members of MatchRequest and Proceeds, the read-only payment_match_rule element, the rental constraints of proceeds and the rental fakes, and it restates no member of the base.
why: The plan gives this key its own CON story while one service can declare its base and its event names only once.
read: RWB-P8-E4043-CON s12.1, s12.3; WP B2-P8-005 story JSON
impact: One document, two owners of parts of it; a duplicate fails the review and the drift test.

text: The rental fields of ProceedsMatched are the case, proceeds and treatment references, the amount, the value date, the match value and the rule identity with its version, and the rental reference and business date are added where no source contradicts them; the two payloads are registered in BACKWARD mode before the app story starts.
why: Only the PaymentMissed example is published, and the rental arm must publish a receipt the case, the treatment and the reporting read model can act on.
read: Architecture v5 slides 22, 42 and 43; TSD P8 T5.3
applied_in: RWB-P8-E4048-APP s12.3; RWB-P8-E4048-CON s7 (AC3, AC4), s12.3
confirm: Solution architect, with the consumers named in 12.3
impact: The event schema is pinned on Day 1; an added optional field stays additive within major version 1.

text: MSG-P8-001 and MSG-P8-002 keep their identifiers and are carried with the placeholder until the Error and Message Standard gives their text; no wording is invented in this run.
why: Both identifiers are in the message set of the feature and neither text is in the read set.
read: FSD P8 A2.9; RWB-E4-048 Validation and messages
impact: Two message rows carry the placeholder; no test asserts the wording.

text: The legacy story carries no approval record and no approved status in the read set, so both stories are written in the Draft (realignment v1) status of Decision D-RCV-60 without a human approval stop.
why: The realignment run proceeds on recorded assumptions instead of approvals.
read: Root AGENTS.md rules 1-14; Template and Rules R1 (U8)
confirm: Portfolio lead at the verification loop
impact: Build status stays Not started and no release date is raised as a gap.

text: The rule identity on the local decision record is the rule_code and rule_version of the payment_match_rule row in force that decided the rental match, and the code of the rental arm is named in no source until the matching-rule story publishes it.
why: The record must name a rule and its version, and the only rule rows this service owns are the payment_match_rule rows.
read: TSD P8 T3.1 (DF-REF-262, DF-REF-263); DP-03; FSD P8 A2.9
applied_in: RWB-P8-E4048-APP s3, s4, s8 (BR4), s13; RWB-P8-E4048-CON s18
confirm: Business analyst, P8, with the rules owner
impact: One record field pair; no rule ID is written in code.
